capability_gaps.gap: SLA accounting supports a business calendar

checks.description: SLA targets are computed from the policy table
checks.detail: P1 opened 09:00Z -> ack 2026-03-02T09:15:00.000Z, resolve 2026-03-02T13:00:00.000Z (policy 15/240 min); P4 -> 2026-03-07T09:00:00.000Z (7200 min). Exact equality is asserted, not "close to", because an off-by-one in the arithmetic is exactly the bug this catches.
checks.oracle_source: calculateSla against a fixed ISO input, exact timestamp equality

checks.description: unknown priority falls back to a default rather than losing the SLA
checks.detail: priority 'NONSENSE' -> P3 (ack 2026-03-02T13:00:00.000Z). A ticket with an unrecognised priority still gets a deadline instead of an undefined one.
checks.oracle_source: calculateSla with an unknown priority label

checks.description: SLA accounting supports a business calendar
checks.detail: NOT IMPLEMENTED. No business-hours, working-day or holiday helper is exported from src/itsm.js, and addMinutes is plain wall-clock arithmetic (itsm.js:22). Consequence: a P1 opened 2026-03-06T23:00:00.000Z (Friday 23:00) gets ackTargetAt 2026-03-06T23:15:00.000Z and is breached true before anyone is on shift. Every SLA number in this project is 24x7. This is recorded as a capability gap, not a bug: 24x7 may well be the intended policy, but the code cannot express business-hours targets, so no one can claim business-hours SLA support from it.
checks.oracle_source: exported symbol scan + calculateSla at a Friday 23:00 boundary

checks.description: closed and cancelled are genuinely terminal, and illegal moves throw
checks.detail: CLOSED outgoing transitions = none (true), CANCELLED -> IN_PROGRESS refused = true, CLOSED->IN_PROGRESS throws = true, legal NEW->ASSIGNED accepted = true. canTransition alone would pass on a state machine nobody enforces, so the throwing path is asserted too.
checks.oracle_source: canTransition + assertTransition over terminal and legal transitions

checks.description: legacy asset statuses map to canonical values, unknown degrades safely
checks.detail: Active->ASSIGNED, In Storage->IN_STOCK, Maintenance->REPAIR, Retired->RETIRED, Lost->LOST (all expected: true); unknown status 'FROBNICATED' -> IN_STOCK, which is a member of ASSET_STATUSES = true. An unknown input falls back to IN_STOCK rather than inventing a value outside the enum.
checks.oracle_source: normalizeAssetRecord over all legacy + one unknown status

checks.description: restore refuses an archive whose payload no longer matches its checksum
checks.detail: sha256 sidecar fa7743601b4a; clean archive restored = true; tampered payload with the ORIGINAL sidecar -> raised Backup integrity check failed: file snapshot.json does not match its .sha256 sidecar. Refusing to restore a tampered or corrupt backup., classified as an integrity refusal = true. Accepting a tampered archive is worse than having no restore at all, because it reports a clean recovery that never happened.
checks.oracle_source: real sha256 sidecar + tampered payload through src/backup.js

checks.description: PowerShell scripts contain no dynamic-evaluation injection shape
checks.detail: scanned 8 .ps1 files against 4 concrete injection shapes (Invoke-Expression/iex, Start-Process -ArgumentList, cmd /c, powershell -Command, ExecutionPolicy Bypass): 0 hits. The suite also runs ps1-lint.js and ps1-syntax.js, both passing. Deliberately NOT counted: unquoted $var in a plain argument, which an earlier naive scan reported 95 of and all were safe forms like Join-Path $DataDir.
checks.oracle_source: 4-shape dynamic-evaluation scan over every .ps1 outside node_modules
